title: mynah-asr serving profile
what_this_is: One question: given THIS box and THIS objective, how should the server be run?
A profile is a contract, not a recommendation. It states the topology, the
settings, the dispatch rows the binary must resolve, the gates a run must
pass, and what was actually measured -- with the date and the conditions.
tools/perf_profile.py turns it into a command line and REFUSES when the world
disagrees with it: a different machine, a dispatch row that resolved to
something else, an environment variable the profile says must be absent.
Why it refuses rather than warns: every capacity number in this repo between
2026-09-18 and 2026-09-20 was taken with the topology typed by hand, and one
of those runs measured a server that had exited on a bad flag while another
measured the wrong model entirely. A configuration that lives in shell
history cannot be compared with itself a week later.

required_keys.dispatch_required: map of --dispatch-map feature -> the value it MUST resolve to
required_keys.measured: what was actually seen, with date and conditions; null until it is

status_values.unmeasured: written from arithmetic or from another box. Nothing was run.
status_values.screened: a WAVE ladder found a ceiling. Screening may disqualify, it never promotes.
status_values.qualified: a SOAK of at least 10 minutes held at the operating point, with transcripts checked.

environment_convention.value: the string the variable must have, or null meaning it must be ABSENT
environment_convention.why: one line. A flag with no reason is a flag nobody can remove later.

notes: A profile belongs to ONE box shape and ONE model. `a` and `b` are functions of
how many cores walk the weights, so a profile does not transfer to a machine
of a different size -- box_advisor refuses to carry constants across a 1.5x
cpu-count difference for the same reason.
Adapted from qwen-tts configs/perf, whose discipline (value+why per variable,
preflight that refuses, status that cannot be claimed) is the part worth copying.
